subject: Encord - Trial Kick Off
text:
Hi all,

Thank you for the time earlier, good to see everyone and I appreciate you
pulling so much of the group together.

A quick recap, plus two things attached that are directly relevant to you.

On the platform, the parts that resonated most with the team were the ones
that address what you found hardest in CVAT: video-native tracking on a
proper timeline, so you are not annotating frame by frame and can see
exactly where a lesion appears across the video; the tracking models and
low latency on that; the built-in review process, so a supervisor can
approve, reject and comment on labels in one place rather than exporting
annotations and reviewing them separately; and the hierarchical
annotations, so you can capture things like tumour grade or stage against a
label rather than being stuck with flat labels..

Two attachments worth your time:

1. Our overview deck, which includes the companies we partner with across
surgical video and medical AI, Moon Surgical, Stryker and Proximie among
them. We built Encord as a video-first platform and have grown through
partnerships with the leading teams in this space, so you would be in good
company.

2. A King's College London study (
https://encord.com/customers/kings-college-london-customer-story/) in which
Encord was benchmarked directly against CVAT on polyp video annotation. It
is about as close a match to your use case as I could hope to share, and it
speaks directly to the question raised on the call about what really
separates us from CVAT on video.

On next steps, I have sent the calendar invite for our kickoff on Wednesday
at 14:30 French time. I have added the colleagues whose email addresses I
already have, so please add anyone from your side I may have missed. If you
are able to share a short, representative video with us, that will let Max
have your environment ready for Wednesday. If sharing your own data is not
straightforward, pointing us to a similar open-source dataset works just as
well, and given tomorrow is a holiday your side, anything you can get to us
today would be a real help.

Looking forward to Wednesday.

Best,
Tom
